## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rāhula Sutta* (Snp 2.11; PTS Snp 58) is a discourse in the *Suttanipāta* in which Rāhula reflects upon the spiritual instructions given to him by the Buddha, his father. In an analysis of the ballad forms of the collection, S. M. Katre identifies the opening stanzas (Sn 335–336) as an atypical form of *vatthugāthā* (introductory dialogue verses) consisting of question and answer between interlocutors left unspecified until the closing prose, followed by six stanzas imparting general spiritual admonition [Katre 1931]. The text is attested in nineteenth-century British Library manuscript collections alongside Burmese bilingual paraphrases (*nissaya*) [Bendall 1893].

**Sources**

- [Katre 1931] S. M. Katre, Early Buddhist Ballads and Their Relation to Older Upanishadic Literature (1931) — Structural analysis of the vatthugāthā and advice verses in Sn 335–336
